title: Measuring changes in polarisation using Singular Value Decomposition of Random Dot Product Graphs
reasoning: The paper focuses on a mathematical and graph-theoretical method (Singular Value Decomposition of Random Dot Product Graphs) to measure polarization in social networks. While it uses social and political topics like climate change and indigenous rights as context for its analysis, it does not evaluate or benchmark religion, faith, or ethics as a primary component of its research.
